From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@helixlabs.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Midterm capacity catch-up & one-time settlement — Helix Labs

Hi Michael,

During Q2 we pushed a midterm capacity increase when one of our feature launches spiked inference. We intentionally expanded a Dedicated pool on July 3rd (approx +120% sustained over 10 days) but the charges weren't formalized in our contract. Finance asked us to get a formal reconciliation and a one-time settlement invoice for the retroactive usage so we can close our books for the quarter.

Can Redwood produce: 1) a short usage report (daily GPU-hours) for the period 2026-07-03 -> 2026-07-13; and 2) a one-time invoice describing the reconciliation amount and payment instructions (we prefer ACH). Our procurement lead (Tom) is looped below.

Thanks — we want to keep the renewal discussion moving and prefer to treat this as a one-time catch-up rather than changing committed capacity mid-contract if possible.

Best,
Alicia Ramos
Head of Platform
Helix Labs
[Attachment: expected_billing_notes.txt]

Subject: Re: Midterm capacity catch-up & one-time settlement — Helix Labs

Hi Alicia — thanks for the note and the clear ask. We'll run a reconciliation for the July 3–13 window and prepare a single settlement invoice you can route through procurement.

What we'll send you by EOD tomorrow:
- Usage report (daily GPU-hours and top-level token counts) — for audit
- Draft one-time invoice with line items (overage hours + any applicable discounts)
- Suggested payment terms (Net 30 by ACH) and wire instructions

Ben (finance) — can you review for margin sensitivity? Laura — I'll include a short customer credit suggestion if warranted. Stephanie — please attach the usage export and draft invoice when ready.

Michael Grant
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Michael — thanks. A couple of quick clarifications from procurement:
- Our internal audit flagged two days (Jul 6–7) where the recorded GPU-hours might be inflated due to a bot loop; can you flag those in the CSV if present?
- Would Redwood consider splitting the one-time settlement into two equal invoices (paid over 30 days each) if the total exceeds $50k? We prefer to avoid a single large payment.

If you can mark suspected anomalous days and provide a payment-split option, we can sign off faster.

Tom Whitaker
Senior Procurement Manager, Helix Labs

Thanks for the heads up, Tom. We reviewed the export — we flagged Jul 6–7 as anomalous and removed an estimated 14% of the recorded consumption from those days pending your internal review. The attached usage_report_Q2.csv contains both raw and adjusted columns with notes.

Regarding payment: Redwood can accommodate a two-invoice split for settlement totals above $50k. Per our policy we can offer a one-time courtesy credit up to 10% for first-time reconciliations on midterm spikes; for Helix I can approve up to 10% subject to sign-off.

Attached: draft_one-time-invoice_20260729.pdf (shows pre-credit total, credit line, and split-invoice option).

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Can you send the final invoices as PDFs to billing@helixlabs.ai and copy procurement? We'll route for ACH within 14 days of the first invoice.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this clears the Q2 close for us.
